title: Fixed-argument exactness of totalized additive bifunctors
statement: Let $C_1,C_2,D$ be preadditive categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], with zero objects and binary biproducts in $C_2,D$. Let $E:C_1\to(C_2\to D)$ be additive separately in both variables. Assume every direct-sum totalization $\operatorname{Tot}_E(P,Q)$ of integer cochain complexes exists. Its degree $n$ is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}E(P^p,Q^q)$ and its differential on the $(p,q)$ summand is $E(d_P,1)+(-1)^pE(1,d_Q)$. Passing chain maps and homotopies through these formulas gives a bifunctor on homotopy categories. For each $P$ in the homotopy category of $C_1$, its fixed-first-argument functor from $K(C_2)$ to $K(D)$ is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category] with the signed integer shift comparison induced by totalization. The homotopy quotient comparison is the one induced by the chain-level totalization.

source.place: definition-cone, definition-distinguished-triangle and proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated (additive-category cone conventions); general totalized-bifunctor proof is the adopted lean/WeilConjectures/FromJoel/Algebra/Homology/BifunctorTriangulated.lean, lines 39-77 and 92-104.

proof.text: Apply the bifunctor termwise and form the direct-sum total with the displayed differential. Additivity and naturality cancel the mixed terms of d squared. Applying the bifunctor to a chain homotopy and inserting the total sign gives a homotopy, so the construction descends to both homotopy quotients. In the varying second variable, extracting an integer shift multiplies the summand of first degree p by (-1)^(np); multiplication of these signs proves the zero and addition laws.

For a chain map f in the second variable, distribute the total coproduct over the two summands of Cone(f). Identify Tot(P,Cone(f)) with Cone(Tot(P,f)), inserting (-1)^p on the summand from the shifted source of f. Direct substitution in the four differential blocks proves it is a chain isomorphism. It intertwines the cone inclusion and the signed boundary using the shift comparison just specified. Thus the image of a standard cone triangle is isomorphic to a standard cone triangle. Passing to homotopy and using invariance of distinguished triangles under isomorphism proves triangulatedness. This is precisely the proved mapping-cone triangle isomorphism and instance in the adopted source file.
